title: CopyCat vs Polly: insurance proposal software compared
summary: Polly handles elementary web proposals. CopyCat generates commercial and personal lines P&C proposals from carrier PDFs, with cited comparisons and policy checking.
body_markdown:
# CopyCat vs Polly


Polly is built for elementary proposals: a self-service template, an interactive web page, a video, and a view tracker. That is fine for a simple personal auto or small-commercial quote. CopyCat is proposal generation software for the P&C work that actually eats an agency’s week: reading multi-carrier commercial and personal lines packets, comparing quotes and renewals with page-level citations, checking bound policies, and producing the proposal in your agency’s own format.


Pick Polly when


Choose Polly for elementary cases: an inexpensive self-service tool to wrap a straightforward personal, life, health, Medicare, or small-commercial quote in an interactive web page with video and view tracking.


Pick CopyCat when


Choose CopyCat when the proposal is real P&C work: multi-line commercial packages, E&S and MGA quotes, home-auto-umbrella bundles, renewals against expiring, bound-policy checks, and a finished proposal in your exact agency format.


Published by CopyCat. This comparison uses vendor documentation, not an independent performance benchmark.


## Side by side

Polly details taken from the company’s own published material, checked September 14, 2026. Sources are listed at the bottom of this page. Products change, so confirm anything that decides your purchase.


## When Polly fits


- You prefer a self-service trial and published subscription pricing.
- Recorded video and knowing when a client opened the proposal matter more than document extraction depth.
- You regularly sell life, health, or Medicare products, which Polly advertises and CopyCat does not currently focus on.
- Your team prefers interactive web delivery and wants to test Polly’s prebuilt proposal templates.


## When CopyCat fits


- Your accounts are past elementary: multi-line commercial packages, E&S placements, and home, auto, and umbrella bundles across several carriers.
- Your team loses time reading commercial carrier PDFs, MGA quotes, E&S documents, schedules, and expiring policies.
- Every value needs to be defensible through a direct link to the page where it was found.
- Your agency wants the output to match its current proposal rather than moving the process into a preset web presentation.
- You need renewal coverage analysis, unlimited comparison columns, or employee benefits Excel workbooks.
- You want commercial policy checking across the full account file, not only proposal presentation.
- You want a customized coverage-gap recommendation added to the editable proposal.


## What CopyCat costs, plainly


A flat monthly fee. No annual contract, no lock-in, no implementation charge, and no per-module add-ons. You can leave whenever. New capabilities ship into the plan you already pay for instead of arriving as upgrades.


Support goes to the team rather than a ticket queue. Most replies come back within minutes, and the commitment is to resolve product issues promptly. Confirm any service-level requirements with us during evaluation.


## Questions buyers actually ask


Is Polly good enough for commercial insurance proposals?


For elementary accounts, often yes: one or two carriers, a single line, and a client who wants a web page and a video. Once an account has multiple lines, E&S or MGA quotes, schedules, or a renewal to compare against expiring, the job becomes reading and reconciling documents. That is the work CopyCat is built for, and where a presentation tool runs out.


What makes CopyCat a strong Polly alternative?


CopyCat goes beyond proposal presentation. It reads complex commercial and personal lines documents, compares coverage with source-page citations, checks bound policies against the complete account file, and adds customized coverage-gap recommendations to an editable agency proposal.


Is CopyCat more expensive than Polly?


Polly publishes a low self-service price of $39 per month or $375 per year. CopyCat asks agencies to contact the team for current pricing because setup includes configuring the agency’s workflow and proposal format. The right comparison is total time removed, not subscription price alone.


Does CopyCat create interactive web proposals or recorded video?


No. Polly is the stronger choice when interactive web delivery, embedded video, and client engagement tracking are the priority. CopyCat focuses on document extraction, cited comparison, editing, and branded proposal or workbook output.


Why do page-level citations matter?


They let a producer or account manager jump from an extracted value to the exact page in the carrier document. That makes review faster and reduces the risk of presenting a number no one can quickly verify.


Can I test CopyCat with the same documents I use in Polly?


Yes. The most useful evaluation is to bring the carrier documents and existing agency template from a real account, then compare the time required, depth of coverage captured, and amount of manual correction needed.


## Test it on the document that normally breaks things


Bring a representative carrier quote packet and your agency’s template. Review the sources, editing workflow, and finished proposal together.
